items.title: Triforest: notice of changed banking details (verify before paying)
items.summary: Landed in info@. Triforest Inc. says its corporate banking details changed effective Sept 16 and asks customers to update remittance records; PDF attached. A bank-detail change is a classic payment-fraud pattern, so confirm by phone with a known Triforest contact before changing anything.

items.title: Ezra Reyes: measure and install timing inquiry
items.summary: Landed in info@. Prospect asks how measurement visits work and whether same-week install is possible when material is in stock. No reply found in info@ Sent Items after 7 days; generic wording, so it may be a low-quality lead.

items.summary: Landed in info@ (Albert also has the earlier thread). Broker asks to drop the $450 disposal charge (they will roll the carpet to the curb) and wants the quote re-sent. Received about 21h ago; no reply found yet.

items.title: Suspicious "invoice" emails with attachments, no body (luxevista)
items.summary: Landed in albert@ and info@. Two near-identical emails ("invice"/"invoice") from a Gmail address with attachments and no text; do not open. A matching Xerox-scan email to info@ (Sept 24) has the same phishing pattern.
